title: Reopen keeps a work order internal after its customer lost the flag
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location has no accounting integration (neither QuickBooks Online nor AccountingHub).
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, closed.
  • After work order 1 was closed, remove customer A's Internal flag (Edit Customer).
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Open the Finance tab.
  3. Open the invoice menu on the Finance tab.
  4. Click "Reopen Work Order".
  5. Click Reopen Work Order in the window.
  6. Click Close Work Order in the work order header.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The document shows.

Step 3:

  • The menu offers "Reopen Work Order".

Step 4:

  • The window opens.

Step 5:

  • The work order is Complete and still shows the "Internal" badge.

Step 6:

  • "Close Work Order" opens the Close confirmation again: it closes as internal.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11758 (Story 1, Turn on Internal Work Orders, flag internal customers, manage categories), story SV-11761 (Story 4, Reopen a closed internal or no-charge work order)

  • S4-E4: “If the customer lost the Internal flag, or the setting was turned off, after Close, Reopen still returns the work order as internal. It closes as internal again (with a new posting date), or the advisor changes the customer to make it billable.”
  • S1-E1: “If a flagged customer loses the flag, its closed internal work orders stay Closed · Internal and its open internal work orders stay internal, in every list and report; the classification is written on the work order, never read from the customer.”
